description: Read-only SQL against Kickoff's STAGING database (kudos_staging) over the Tunnelblick VPN. Not production.

stage_guide.description: [STAGING kudos_staging, not production] What the staging database holds, when to use it instead of the production routes (Kickoff Sanitized DB, zdr_ask), core tables, definitions and limits. Read once before an unfamiliar question.

stage_tables.description: [STAGING kudos_staging, not production] List tables with approximate row counts. like: a LIKE pattern on the table name ("%call%"; a bare word matches anywhere). column_like: only tables having a column like it, listing those columns ("coach_id").

stage_describe.description: [STAGING kudos_staging, not production] Columns, types, indexes and foreign keys for one table or up to 10 in one call (tables: [...]). Wide tables (clients has ~150 columns): pass column_like to see only the columns you need.

column_like.description: only columns (and their indexes and keys) like this, e.g. %coach% or insurance

stage_query.description: [STAGING kudos_staging, not production] Run one read statement (SELECT, WITH, SHOW, EXPLAIN, DESCRIBE). Prefer aggregates. Use ? placeholders with params for values. Shows 100 rows by default (limit up to 1000) as a column list plus one JSON array per row. For more rows than you need to read, pass output_path (.csv/.tsv/.jsonl, absolute, git-ignored if inside a repo; name only the columns you need) to stream up to 5,000,000 rows to a file; the answer is counts and a sample.

output_path.description: write every row to this file instead of showing them

stage_status.description: [STAGING kudos_staging, not production] VPN state, database user, read-only check, latency, newest migration. Use when a call fails or before a long session.
